My wife and I took a trip to Waterton National Park in Southern Alberta. We hiked from Waterton Townsite 2.5 KM to Bertha Bay. After setting up camp we decided to go for a hike to explore before dinner. We took a steep hike up to Bertha Lake which is a 3.6 KM roundtrip. When we got there we had a small snack, relaxed a bit and turned around to go back. As we were coming down we saw a couple with no gear at all. As we were heading down the trail I had my head down because I was tired and just wanted to get back to camp. My wife shouted "Nevets!" and I look up and there is a grizzly about ten or so meters away coming up the trail. We nearly panicked but backed away slowly instead. We backed away for about two minutes but what seemed like forever because the bear kept coming up the trail. Eventually the bear left the trail (I guess it wasn't convenient for it anymore). We met up with the couple we left behind and went back down again. Pretty exciting time for us. *PS the hike was way better than the lake itself.

We slept at Bertha Bay for a night, packed up and continued on to Boundary Bay (3.4 KM hike). Both sites were nicely wooded and within sight of Upper Waterton Lake. When we got to the site we immediately set up camp and took a nap. Woke up and found a deer milling around. It was cool because we got a ton of close up pics but it was kind of disturbing because the deer didn't seem to have a healthy fear of humans. I guess people have been feeding them. It was cool to see the actual boundary between the States and Canada. They actually have it clear cut and if you climb a hill you can see the line as though you were looking at a map. Anyway, it was a great trip and very quiet. At both sites we were the only people actually camping there. We saw a few people hiking but for the most part we were the only ones out there.

TL;DR: Went camping in Waterton National Park for three nights. Excellent trip. Encountered a bear. Now I want to hear about the best trips you've had!

Its so hard to pick an absolute favorite, but I'll share my favorite bear encounter. While hiking in the New Mexico Pecos Wilderness with a group of 6 pals we met up with a New Mexico ranger traveling with a burro. So the ranger (Travis) had little else to do but travel along with us which was awesome because each morning he'd allow us to pack a certain amount of weight onto his burro and of course he knew of all the best routes. Travis wears this dope Indiana Jones hat, carries a tomahawk, and proves to be an all-around cool dude.

When we dropped packs for lunch on the third day traveling with Travis a bear appeared and began to approach us. We all just sat and watched but as soon the burro made a noise Travis just says to us "hold my hat" and busts off chasing this black bear down with his tomahawk. It was easily the most vivid display of manliness I've witnessed in person. Travis split off later that afternoon and we hiked for another incredible week. Still, meeting that guy on the trail and getting to know him the little bit that we did is one of all our favorite stories to tell. Travis was seriously one bad motherfucker.

I'm only 19 and am currently attending university but I have had my career decided for over 9 years now and have worked hard to (hopefully) assure my place in the industry. I intend to be a professional game developer therefore I am majoring in Game Development at one of the top game dev schools in the world, Rochester Institute of Technology.

I started pretty young by being introduced to video games and board games at probably around the age of 5 thanks to my wonderfully nerdy father. By 10 I started to use Game Maker and started doing pixel art for both my games and other games for people on the YoYo games forum. Within a year I began to dive into Game Maker Language (GML) and took all the programming books my father had. They were mostly old books on C and C++ and I tried to my best to read them and gain whatever I could from them. I won't lie, I barely understood them but that was the drive I had and I wanted to learn. While using Game Maker and RPG Maker I also began making Source Engine maps for Half Life 2, Garrysmod, CS:S, etc. Map making became a hobby of mine and I really enjoy it to today although I haven't released a map in a long time. Also at the time I began using Blender to introduce myself to 3D Modeling and since then I still haven't gotten much better at it but I would love to.

At 14 in highschool I took a basic programming course that taught me python. Then by about 15 I got started with C# and XNA. I did various hobby projects and of course a full remake of pong with menus, sound, gameplay, etc. At 16 I learned Java thanks to taking a computer science course in High School. My professor tried to talk me out of specializing so soon at university by majoring in game development instead of something like computer science but it didn't work. I knew I probably would be payed less, I knew I might not have the same job security, and I knew I would probably have to put in worse hours but it didn't matter to me, I've always wanted to make games.

During highschool I interned for two years at a local software company that made inventory management software for warehouses. I was a quality assurance intern and learned about how software is created within large teams and how bugs and problems are monitored and resolved. There I created internal software with Python, HTML, and CSS to monitor the wide array of virtual machines that were constantly running in our server room.

Recently during my first semester at university I taught myself Javascript and how to use the Phaser game API to create a incremental and randomized space SHMUP that would run in your browser. The project eventually became too large for me to manage and had quite a few bugs so I gave up. However after that I began my current project and one of the first to really see the light of day. Using C# and Unity I began development of Unlimited Golf, a randomly generated 2D golf game that will be coming to your web browser and an app store near you in a month or two! You can actually help me out and provide some feedback at /v/playmygame and the game has its own sub at /v/unlimitedgolf!

Sorry I just wrote practically my life story but I have been passionate about my "career" for almost as long as I can remember.

TL;DR I have been making games and aiming for a game development career for years. GML, then Python, C#, Java, Javascript, and finally Unity. I am going to release my first commercial game in a month or two and you can check it out at /v/playmygame and /v/unlimitedgolf.
